I’ve had really rough luck with US Bank. Despite having multiple cards with 30k, 40k, 50k limits, my USBAR was initially $5k. After a year or so I tried to get a limit increase and I finally got it to $10k. As I was maxing out the card I tried another CLI 6 months ago and got zilch with a credit score of 780 something and 0 hard inquiries.

A week ago I applied for the Smartly and got $20k. What could it have been that was different?

  1. My current credit limit utilization of the USBAR card was low (I don’t carry a balance but I also wasn’t buying furniture from costco this time so it was under). Previously I had tried to get it very high, which I had heard is often useful for issuers (I’ve had auto-CLI from barclay’s for instance with heavy spend).
  2. I had had a 30 day delinquency 6 years ago that fell off (always make sure your rarely used cards are on autopay before going on a long trip!)- this with some lower credit usage bumped my score to 810.
  3. I had simultaneously asked for a CLI from both Fidelity and the USBAR. Both are underwritten by Elan. My Fidelity limit is 50k. Maybe Elan looked at both and didn’t feel comfortable giving more and denied both.

I would search around forums because I recall some people getting significant USBank limits. I think USBank is like a very skittish animal and you have to woo them. So I think:

  1. Get CL usage way, way down across the board while showing you use the card. Especially for your Smartly that may involve simultaneously putting on a lot of spend for a few months, paying it off repeatedly midcycle, then letting it chill for a month or two with $0. You may have some leeway with exceeding the credit limit as well by some amount.
  2. Let hard inquiries fall off or age out at least 6 months.
  3. If you have a significant balance with them, good.

As a counterpoint, I had no relation with them except for a Fidelity card if you count that (and perhaps a transit benefit card and a work travel card). In any case, I got a 23k credit line last week.

Answering my own question, US Bank has no monthly limits on savings, you can use it exactly like a checking and make some interest on it.

For Alliant, I think an ACH transfer counts, it doesn’t have to be a real direct deposit. You can probably do a recurring $1 transfer each month.

Putting $10k in Smartly checking loses you $9,000 * 4% = $360 of interest. I am using 4% as the rough benchmark of interest rate at other banks/T-bills. This hasn’t taken into account that for the $1,000 in Alliant, you still get 0.25% of interest vs. $10,000 in Smartly Checking that only has 0.005% of interest.
